(1) the machine learning is not able to reach the total autonomy; (2) the human is still in the centre of the manufacturing singuality; (3) the intelligent machine architecture towards manufacturing singularity is proposed; (4) the intelligent machine has embedded ML modules in multiple learning loop; and (5) the human is the centre of the intelligent machine architecture.

the following issues: (a) the question of the human role in the future; (b) the question of manufacturing singularity; (c) the question of an intelligent machine architecture.

the thesis on total automation is false, and that there is a need for a new architecture of intelligent machines, which would be human dependent and would have embedded ML functionality.
the human is still in the centre of CPS and I4.0, but the role of human will change from a direct decision maker, to a designer, developer, and maintainer of the intelligent machine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intelligent machines will be always human-dependent and that the manufacturing singularity will be achieved by intelligent machines, but not by the total automation.

the intelligent machines will be human dependent and that the human will remain as the centre of the CPS and I4.0, and that the manufacturing singularity will be reached when the human will be able to control the CPS and I 4.0 in a way that the CPS will be able to perform all the tasks that are necessary for manufacturing.

, in our view, the manufacturing singularity will be reached when a machine will be able to learn, in the context of manufacturing systems, to the same level as a human, but that it is not possible to reach this singularity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, although the machine learning algorithms will be able to learn and to make decisions in the context of the CPS, the human role will not be eliminated, because there is a limit in the autonomy of the ML algorithms.

the intelligent machine architecture is not the same as the architecture of a robot, but that there is a difference, namely that the intelligent machine is not a robot but a system of robots and other intelligent devices (sensors, actuators, etc.).

the human will remain the centre of intelligent manufacturing systems and that the manufacturing singularity does not mean total automation, and, consequently, total exclusion of human from the decision making process.
